text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
NeedsMoney(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
AtMarySchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
Hannah :: a specific individual.

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoney(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school work in student jobs on campus, then they need to earn money.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school order takeout frequently, then they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrdersTakeoutFrequently(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People order takeout frequently or enjoy the dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, then they spend a lot of time eating and catching up in the dining halls.
AtMarySchool(hannah) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school.
WorksInStudentJobs(hannah) ::: Hannah works in student jobs on campus.
∀x (NeedsMoney(x) → (¬PickyEater(x) ∧ NeedsMoney(x))) ::: If she needs to earn money, then she is not a picky eater and needs money.

Conclusion:
AtMarySchool(hannah) ∧ ¬PickyEater(hannah) ∧ SpendsTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(hannah) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school, is not a picky eater, and spends a lot of time in the dining halls.
